internal_discovery.plain_explanation: Across all 148 occurrences the root turns on clear perceptual grasp - 'seeing' in the sense of actually apprehending, not merely aiming the eyes. It names the sight-faculty and eyes (abSaar), the gaze/glance and its acuity (baSar), the keen perceiver (baSiir - the same intensive word covers a man's plain eyesight vs blindness and God's total perception of deeds), and the perceiving act (abSara/baSura). The text itself carries this into the mind: whoever is given proofs and 'sees' (abSara) vs whoever is 'blind' (6:104); eyes do not go blind but hearts do (22:46). But a coherent minority pushes the other way - baSaa'ir/tabSira are revelation as 'clear proofs', the day is mubSir ('sight-giving', though it does not itself see), and baSiira at 75:14 is a 'proof against oneself'. There the root denotes being/making-evident rather than perceiving, which is why a single narrow uniform gloss cannot be graded higher than MODERATE.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: bSr is bounded away from: (1) naZar/looking-toward - 7:198 and 10:43 affirm they LOOK (yanZuruuna/yanZuru) yet deny they baSr (laa yubSiruuna): orientation without uptake; (2) the eye-organ 'ayn - 7:195 'a'yunun yubSiruuna bihaa' and 36:66 destroy the a'yun so 'how would they yubSiruuna': the organ is 'ayn, bSr is its function; (3) hearing - held as the vision half of sam'/baSar (17:36); (4) heart-comprehension (fiqh/'aql) - 22:46/7:179 set blind abSaar/eyes beside uncomprehending quluub; (5) moral rightness - 20:96 the Samiri 'baSurtu' perceives yet sins, 21:3 they 'tubSiruuna' sorcery.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: 75:14 «بَلِ ٱلْإِنسَٰنُ عَلَىٰ نَفْسِهِۦ بَصِيرَةٌ»: baSiira is predicated OF a person and denotes a self-evident proof/witness against the self, that-which-makes-manifest, not an agent perceiving nor a faculty of perception. It inverts the agentive perceiver-sense into the evidentiary object-sense and is accommodated only by broadening the nucleus toward 'clarity in either direction'.
internal_discovery.strongest_competitor: Rival: bSr is two Quran-internally distinguishable lexical fields on one root, not one live synchronic sense - (F1) SENSORY (baSar, abSaar-eyes, abSara/yubSir, baSiir-seer, divine baSiir) vs (F2) EVIDENTIARY/FACTITIVE (baSaa'ir, baSiira-as-proof at 75:14, tabSira, mubSir-sign/day, causative baSSara), where baSaa'ir never denotes physical eyes though morphologically parallel to abSaar, and mubSir/baSiira invert the perceiver sense into make/be-evident. It is rejected as a full partition because the text explicitly bridges the poles in single verses - 6:104 welds baSaa'ir (proof) to abSara (see) to 'amiya (blind); 22:46 carries abSaar into hearts' blindness; 13:16 equates a'maa/baSiir with Zulumaat/nuur; 'uwli al-abSaar' uses the eye-plural for discernment. So it is one bridged derivational family, not homonyms - but the F2 valence is real and caps the uniform claim at MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE rather than STRONG/UNIVERSAL.

internal_discovery.rationale: All three lenses independently converge on a single visual-apprehension nucleus that is broad (148/148 forms), distinctive (the naZar-vs-bSr boundary at 7:198/10:43 and the 'ayn-vs-yubSir instrument frame at 7:195/36:66 are clean, unforced, adversarially-strong wins) and internally bridged across sensory and cognitive poles (6:104, 22:46, 13:16), so RESISTANT/UNRESOLVED (no nucleus) is not honestly sustainable and PREFERRED is warranted. But STRONG/UNIVERSAL is barred by a coherent resistant lexicalized/factitive sub-class - baSaa'ir/baSiira-as-proof (75:14)/tabSira/mubSir/baSSara - where the root denotes being-or-making-evident rather than an agent perceiving, and unifying both poles requires an abstraction wide enough to trip the 'fits-everything' caution. Per contract, a resistant lexicalized/nominal sub-class caps strength at MODERATE and scope at REPRESENTATIVE; kind is DERIVATIONAL_FAMILY because the poles are morphology-conditioned extensions of one root, bridged Quran-internally, not a forced unity of unbridged homonyms.

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: abSaar (pl. N) = the sight-faculty/eyes-as-organ-by-metonymy and the act of sight: given/created, sealed, snatched, lowered, humbled, fixed in dread; metonymically 'uwli al-abSaar' = possessors of discernment.
clusters.classification_rationale: Plural noun consistently naming the perceptual faculty/organ-function; paired with sam' (10:31,16:78,32:9,67:23), lowered as gaze (24:30/31), and carried metaphorically to discernment (3:13,24:44,59:2,38:45). 'laa tudrikuhu al-abSaar' 6:103 shows it names grasping-perception, not the bare eyeball.
clusters.supporting_evidence_note: 22:46 'laa ta'maa al-abSaar wa laakin ta'maa al-quluub' explicitly bridges the sensory plural into cognition - a key internal weld against a homonym split.

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: baSar (sg. N) = the act/faculty of sight foregrounding directedness and acuity: the glance ('lamH al-baSar'), keen sight ('baSaruka al-yawma Hadiid'), directed scanning that returns dulled (67:3-4), non-swerving fixation (53:17), dazzlement (75:7).
clusters.classification_rationale: Singular noun stressing directed acute looking and its keenness/defeasibility; listed as an accountable faculty beside sam' and fu'aad (17:36).
clusters.supporting_evidence_note: 50:22 'fa-baSaruka al-yawma Hadiid' thematizes acuity (keen apprehension), distinguishing bSr from mere eye-aim.

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: baSiir (intensive) = 'one who perceives keenly' - the divine All-Perceiving-of-deeds (usually paired sami'/khabiir, complement 'bimaa ta'maluuna/bil-'ibaad') and, in identical form, the human 'sighted one' vs the blind (a'maa) and restored eyesight.
clusters.classification_rationale: One intensive lexeme spanning God's total awareness (2:110,17:1,57:4...) and a man's plain eyesight (12:93,12:96,20:125; 'hal yastawii al-a'maa wal-baSiir'), showing baSiir encodes 'keen perceiver', not an organ.
clusters.supporting_evidence_note: 13:16 sets a'maa/baSiir alongside Zulumaat/nuur, and 12:93/12:96 restore literal baSar - the same word covers optical and total perception, unified as keen apprehension.

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Form IV abSara/yubSir/tubSir and Form I baSura = to see/perceive/realize/discern: overwhelmingly perception (often negated failure-to-perceive despite eyes), cognitive realization ('abSarnaa', 'faman abSara'), exclamative intensification ('abSir bihi'), and Form I 'special noticing' of what others miss (20:96, 28:11).
clusters.classification_rationale: Finite/imperative verbs of the perceiving act; the instrument frame 'a'yunun yubSiruuna bihaa' (7:195) and 'laTamsnaa 'alaa a'yunihim fa-annaa yubSiruuna' (36:66) fix bSr as the eye's function, not the eye.
clusters.supporting_evidence_note: 7:198 'tarahum yanZuruuna ilayka wa hum laa yubSiruuna' and 10:43 make naZar (looking) vs bSr (apprehending) an explicit Quran-internal boundary.

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Cognitive perceiver-side extension: baSiira '(acting) upon clear insight' (12:108 'alaa baSiira) and mustabSiriin 'possessed of discerning sight' (29:38, yet led astray).
clusters.classification_rationale: Both denote a perceiver's clarity of discernment (insight), a smooth morphology-driven extension of 'keen apprehension' that remains agent-side, distinct from the evidentiary object-sense.
clusters.supporting_evidence_note: 29:38 'wa kaanuu mustabSiriin' = they could see clearly yet were misled - perception without rectitude, consistent with the moral-neutrality boundary.

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: That-which-is-or-makes-evident (a distinct, largely factitive/nominal valence): baSaa'ir = 'clear proofs / means of insight' (revelation-objects), baSiira-as-proof (75:14 'a witness against oneself'), tabSira = 'an enlightening / making-see' (50:8), mubSir(a) = 'sight-giving day / self-evidencing sign' (inanimate subject), causative baSSara 'to be shown' (70:11).
clusters.classification_rationale: These invert or shift the dominant 'X perceives Y' valence: baSaa'ir denotes proof-objects and never physical eyes though parallel to abSaar; mubSir is active in form but factitive in sense (the day/sign does not perceive); 75:14 makes baSiira a proof, not a perceiving. They are bridged to the nucleus (6:104 collocates baSaa'ir + abSara + 'amiya) but carry a different denotation/valence, so a single uniform sense cannot absorb them without over-abstraction.
clusters.supporting_evidence_note: 6:104 'qad jaa'akum baSaa'ir min rabbikum faman abSara falinafsihi wa man 'amiya' binds the proof-noun to the seeing-verb and blindness - the internal bridge that keeps this a sub-class of one family rather than an unbridged homonym; yet 45:20/28:43/17:102 (baSaa'ir as Scripture), 50:8 (tabSira) and 10:67/27:86/40:61 (al-nahaar mubSiran) show the make/be-evident valence that caps the uniform claim.

reconciliation.rationale: Retained as a resistant seam: it is Quran-internally connected to the family (baSiira shares the make-clear field of baSaa'ir/6:104), so it does not force UNRESOLVED, but its evidentiary predication genuinely resists the uniform perceiver-sense and is the decisive reason strength is capped at MODERATE.

Reconciled as a factitive/enabling valence within the family (supported by causative baSSara 70:11 and tabSira 50:8): not resistant to the ROOT field, but a distinct valence that a single narrow gloss covers only by abstraction - hence STRUCTURAL_UNCERTAINTY, not RESISTANT.

The same verse welds baSaa'ir to the seeing-verb abSara and to 'amiya (blindness), proving the evidentiary nominal is a bridged extension of the sight nucleus rather than an unbridged homonym; the class is kept as a bridged sub-family (DERIVATIONAL_FAMILY), not a partition.

adversarial_verification.notes: The perceptual-apprehension core is broad, distinctive (naZar-vs-bSr 7:198/10:43; 'ayn-vs-yubSir 7:195/36:66) and adversarially clean, and the sensory<->cognitive bridge is Quran-internal (6:104,22:46,13:16), so the core is not refuted (not FAILED) and RESISTANT/no-nucleus is not sustainable. But a coherent resistant lexicalized/factitive sub-class (baSaa'ir/baSiira-as-proof/tabSira/mubSir) genuinely resists a UNIFORM sense, so a clean SUPPORTED-with-empty-failing-occurrences run cannot be claimed: status is NOT_RUN with the resisting occurrences recorded.

occurrence_dispositions.note: These invert or shift the dominant 'X perceives Y' valence: baSaa'ir denotes proof-objects and never physical eyes though parallel to abSaar; mubSir is active in form but factitive in sense (the day/sign does not perceive); 75:14 makes baSiira a proof, not a perceiving. occurrence_dispositions.note: These invert or shift the dominant 'X perceives Y' valence: baSaa'ir denotes proof-objects and never physical eyes though parallel to abSaar; mubSir is active in form but factitive in sense (the day/sign does not perceive); 75:14 makes baSiira a proof, not a perceiving. They are bridged to the nucleus (6:104 collocates baSaa'ir + abSara + 'amiya) but carry a different denotation/valence, so a single uniform sense cannot absorb them without over-abstraction.
occurrence_dispositions.candidate_semantic_interpretation: That-which-is-or-makes-evident (a distinct, largely factitive/nominal valence): baSaa'ir = 'clear proofs / means of insight' (revelation-objects), baSiira-as-proof (75:14 'a witness against oneself'), tabSira = 'an enlightening / making-see' (50:8), mubSir(a) = 'sight-giving day / self-evidencing sign' (inanimate subject), causative baSSara 'to be shown' (70:11).
occurrence_dispositions.cluster_supporting_evidence: 6:104 'qad jaa'akum baSaa'ir min rabbikum faman abSara falinafsihi wa man 'amiya' binds the proof-noun to the seeing-verb and blindness - the internal bridge that keeps this a sub-class of one family rather than an unbridged homonym; yet 45:20/28:43/17:102 (baSaa'ir as Scripture), 50:8 (tabSira) and 10:67/27:86/40:61 (al-nahaar mubSiran) show the make/be-evident valence that caps the uniform claim.

occurrence_dispositions.note: al-nahaar mubSiran: Form-IV active participle predicated of an inanimate non-perceiving subject (the day), forcing a factitive 'sight-enabling' reading - a valence the dominant finite 'X perceives Y' pattern does not carry (cf. 10:67, 27:86, tabSira 50:8, causative baSSara 70:11). | al-nahaar mubSiran (10:67, 27:86, 40:61): an active participle of a perception verb is predicated of a non-perceiving subject, requiring a causative/enabling reading (supported by causative baSSara 70:11 and tabSira 50:8).
occurrence_dispositions.candidate_semantic_interpretation: That-which-is-or-makes-evident (a distinct, largely factitive/nominal valence): baSaa'ir = 'clear proofs / means of insight' (revelation-objects), baSiira-as-proof (75:14 'a witness against oneself'), tabSira = 'an enlightening / making-see' (50:8), mubSir(a) = 'sight-giving day / self-evidencing sign' (inanimate subject), causative baSSara 'to be shown' (70:11).
occurrence_dispositions.cluster_supporting_evidence: 6:104 'qad jaa'akum baSaa'ir min rabbikum faman abSara falinafsihi wa man 'amiya' binds the proof-noun to the seeing-verb and blindness - the internal bridge that keeps this a sub-class of one family rather than an unbridged homonym; yet 45:20/28:43/17:102 (baSaa'ir as Scripture), 50:8 (tabSira) and 10:67/27:86/40:61 (al-nahaar mubSiran) show the make/be-evident valence that caps the uniform claim.
occurrence_dispositions.preliminary_note: These invert or shift the dominant 'X perceives Y' valence: baSaa'ir denotes proof-objects and never physical eyes though parallel to abSaar; mubSir is active in form but factitive in sense (the day/sign does not perceive); 75:14 makes baSiira a proof, not a perceiving. They are bridged to the nucleus (6:104 collocates baSaa'ir + abSara + 'amiya) but carry a different denotation/valence, so a single uniform sense cannot absorb them without over-abstraction.
occurrence_dispositions.reconciliation_rationale: Reconciled as a factitive/enabling valence within the family (supported by causative baSSara 70:11 and tabSira 50:8): not resistant to the ROOT field, but a distinct valence that a single narrow gloss covers only by abstraction - hence STRUCTURAL_UNCERTAINTY, not RESISTANT.

occurrence_dispositions.note: These invert or shift the dominant 'X perceives Y' valence: baSaa'ir denotes proof-objects and never physical eyes though parallel to abSaar; mubSir is active in form but factitive in sense (the day/sign does not perceive); 75:14 makes baSiira a proof, not a perceiving. They are bridged to the nucleus (6:104 collocates baSaa'ir + abSara + 'amiya) but carry a different denotation/valence, so a single uniform sense cannot absorb them without over-abstraction.
occurrence_dispositions.candidate_semantic_interpretation: That-which-is-or-makes-evident (a distinct, largely factitive/nominal valence): baSaa'ir = 'clear proofs / means of insight' (revelation-objects), baSiira-as-proof (75:14 'a witness against oneself'), tabSira = 'an enlightening / making-see' (50:8), mubSir(a) = 'sight-giving day / self-evidencing sign' (inanimate subject), causative baSSara 'to be shown' (70:11).
occurrence_dispositions.cluster_supporting_evidence: 6:104 'qad jaa'akum baSaa'ir min rabbikum faman abSara falinafsihi wa man 'amiya' binds the proof-noun to the seeing-verb and blindness - the internal bridge that keeps this a sub-class of one family rather than an unbridged homonym; yet 45:20/28:43/17:102 (baSaa'ir as Scripture), 50:8 (tabSira) and 10:67/27:86/40:61 (al-nahaar mubSiran) show the make/be-evident valence that caps the uniform claim.

occurrence_dispositions.verse_text: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَهَاجَرُوا۟ وَجَٰهَدُوا۟ بِأَمْوَٰلِهِمْ وَأَنفُسِهِمْ فِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَاوَوا۟ وَّنَصَرُوٓا۟ أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلِيَآءُ بَعْضٍ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَلَمْ يُهَاجِرُوا۟ مَا لَكُم مِّن وَلَٰيَتِهِم مِّن شَىْءٍ حَتَّىٰ يُهَاجِرُوا۟ وَإِنِ ٱسْتَنصَرُوكُمْ فِى ٱلدِّينِ فَعَلَيْكُمُ ٱلنَّصْرُ إِلَّا عَلَىٰ قَوْمٍۭ بَيْنَكُمْ وَبَيْنَهُم مِّيثَٰقٌ وَٱللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ

resistant_deep_analysis.preliminary_note: These invert or shift the dominant 'X perceives Y' valence: baSaa'ir denotes proof-objects and never physical eyes though parallel to abSaar; mubSir is active in form but factitive in sense (the day/sign does not perceive); 75:14 makes baSiira a proof, not a perceiving. They are bridged to the nucleus (6:104 collocates baSaa'ir + abSara + 'amiya) but carry a different denotation/valence, so a single uniform sense cannot absorb them without over-abstraction.
resistant_deep_analysis.reconciliation_rationale: Retained as a resistant seam: it is Quran-internally connected to the family (baSiira shares the make-clear field of baSaa'ir/6:104), so it does not force UNRESOLVED, but its evidentiary predication genuinely resists the uniform perceiver-sense and is the decisive reason strength is capped at MODERATE.

independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A,B,C) converged: A and C graded MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE; B graded STRONG only for the narrow 'single-nucleus / non-unbridged' structural claim and explicitly conceded MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE for any claim of uniform meaning.
candidate_root_contribution: bSr = visually-grounded clear apprehension - the discerning uptake of an object paradigmatically by eyesight, together with its faculty/organ-by-metonymy (abSaar), its act/gaze (baSar), its keen agent (baSiir, incl. God as all-Perceiving-of-deeds) and its verbal act (abSara/baSura = to see/perceive/discern) - extended by morphology, and bridged Quran-internally, to insight/discernment and, on a distinct valence, to that-which-is-or-makes-evident (baSaa'ir/baSiira-as-proof, tabSira, mubSir sight-enabling day/sign, causative baSSara). NOT mere eye-direction (naZar), NOT the eye-organ ('ayn), NOT bare knowledge ('ilm), NOT moral rectitude.

layer_attribution.occurrence_evidence: 148/148 occurrences read across all 8 qac buckets; sensory faculty/act (abSaar,baSar), keen perceiver (baSiir), perceiving verbs (abSara/baSura), and the evidentiary/factitive minority (baSaa'ir,baSiira,tabSira,mubSir,baSSara,mustabSir) each anchored to explicit word_refs and verse_text.
layer_attribution.derivation: Morphology systematically modulates one root field: pl./sg. nouns = faculty/act; intensive baSiir = keen agent; Form IV/I = perceiving act; Form II/N(IV)/N(II) = causative/factitive 'make-see/be-evident'; N(X) = discerning capacity - extensions, not homonyms.
layer_attribution.lexical_class: A resistant lexicalized/nominal sub-class exists - baSaa'ir/baSiira-as-proof(75:14)/tabSira denoting 'clear proof/insight' as objects, plus factitive mubSir/baSSara - carrying a make/be-evident denotation distinct from 'an agent perceives'.
layer_attribution.contextual_relation: Narrative/contextual senses (Samiri's illicit discernment 20:96; Jacob's restored eyesight 12:93/96; eschatological fixed/humbled abSaar 21:97,79:9; lowered gaze 24:30-31) are occurrence-level colourings and are NOT elevated into the root claim.
layer_attribution.reconciliation: Preliminary 'separate evidentiary class' and 'mubSir resists' readings were reconciled to a bridged DERIVATIONAL_FAMILY via 6:104/22:46/13:16; 75:14 alone is retained as a genuine RESISTANT seam rather than forced into unity.
layer_attribution.unresolved_resistance: The evidentiary/factitive valence (esp. 75:14 baSiira-as-proof and al-nahaar mubSiran) resists a single narrow uniform sense; this residual, bridged but non-uniform, is the basis for MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE rather than STRONG/UNIVERSAL, and is recorded, not erased.

hard_cases.reason: baSiira predicated of a person = a self-evident proof/witness against the self, inverting the agentive perceiver-sense into the evidentiary object-sense.

evidence_basis.statement: 75:14 «بَلِ ٱلْإِنسَٰنُ عَلَىٰ نَفْسِهِۦ بَصِيرَةٌ»: baSiira is predicated OF a person and denotes a self-evident proof/witness against the self, that-which-makes-manifest, not an agent perceiving nor a faculty of perception. It inverts the agentive perceiver-sense into the evidentiary object-sense and is accommodated only by broadening the nucleus toward 'clarity in either direction'.

hard_cases.reason: baSaa'ir denotes Scripture/proof-objects for people, morphologically parallel to abSaar yet never physical eyes - the make/be-evident valence.

evidence_basis.statement: 45:20/28:43/17:102/7:203: baSaa'ir denotes revelation as 'clear proofs' (patterned with hudan wa raHma), an object-sense that never means physical eyes though parallel to abSaar - a bridged (6:104) but distinct-denotation sub-class.

hard_cases.reason: Form-IV active participle 'mubSiran' predicated of the inanimate day forces a factitive 'sight-enabling' sense the dominant perceiver valence does not carry.

evidence_basis.statement: al-nahaar mubSiran (10:67, 27:86, 40:61): an active participle of a perception verb is predicated of a non-perceiving subject, requiring a causative/enabling reading (supported by causative baSSara 70:11 and tabSira 50:8).

hard_cases.reason: Same subjects LOOK (yanZuruuna) yet do NOT baSr (laa yubSiruuna): distinctiveness test separating bSr (uptake) from naZar (orientation).

evidence_basis.statement: 7:198 'tarahum yanZuruuna ilayka wa hum laa yubSiruuna' and 10:43 make naZar (looking) vs bSr (apprehending) an explicit Quran-internal boundary.

hard_cases.reason: The Samiri perceives ('baSurtu') a hidden trace yet sins - bSr is morally neutral, not rightness of object.

evidence_basis.statement: 20:96 'baSurtu bimaa lam yabSuruu bihi': Form-I discernment of a hidden trace by a wrongdoer - perception without moral rectitude, evidencing the negative boundary (bSr != rightness of object).

hard_case_representation.rationale: A preferred nucleus holds, so this is not an unresolved multi-class root; the hard cases are evidence-derived seams and boundaries. Two are RESISTANT_SEAMs (75:14, 45:20) marking the evidentiary/factitive sub-class that caps strength at MODERATE; one is a form-meaning STRUCTURAL_ATYPICALITY (40:61); two are ADVERSARIAL_BOUNDARY distinctiveness tests (7:198 naZar-vs-bSr, 20:96 moral neutrality). Each statement also appears as the strongest_counterexample or as a cluster/override note.

rejection_condition.challenging_finding: A Quran-internal demonstration that the evidentiary/factitive derivatives (baSaa'ir, baSiira-as-proof 75:14, tabSira 50:8, mubSir day/sign) share NO bridge with the perceiving forms - i.e. that they form an unbridged separate lexical field - which would break the DERIVATIONAL_FAMILY unity and force UNRESOLVED_CLASS_ONLY.
rejection_condition.search_location: Verses collocating an evidentiary/factitive form with a perceiving form or its antonym: 6:104 (baSaa'ir + abSara + 'amiya), 22:46 (abSaar + qalb-blindness), 13:16 (baSiir/a'maa + nuur/Zulumaat), and every baSaa'ir/mubSir/tabSira context.
rejection_condition.verification_method: Test whether any perceiving-verb, baSiir, or a'maa/blindness antonym co-occurs with the evidentiary/factitive nominals; absence of ALL such bridges across the sub-class would support the partition claim.
rejection_condition.confounder_control: Exclude mere shared root/morphology and translation-driven glosses as evidence of bridging; require an actual same-context Quranic collocation, not a lexicon-supplied synonymy.
rejection_condition.failure_consequence: If an unbridged partition is demonstrated, downgrade to research_state=UNRESOLVED, result_strength=UNRESOLVED, claim_scope=LOCAL, claim_scope_kind=UNRESOLVED_CLASS_ONLY, and stop asserting a single nucleus.

reopen_conditions: If baSaa'ir or tabSira is found in a context that anchors it to a literal eye/organ (not proof/insight), collapsing the evidentiary sub-class into the sensory pole and permitting a stronger uniform claim.

If a Form-IV finite occurrence of abSara/yubSir is shown to require the factitive 'make-evident' sense (as mubSir does), or conversely if mubSir is shown to require an agentive 'perceiver' sense at 10:67/27:86/40:61, changing the valence split.
If the naZar-vs-bSr contrast (7:198, 10:43) is undercut by an occurrence where yubSir means bare eye-direction without apprehension, dissolving the core distinctiveness boundary.

falsification_evidence.status_rationale: The perceptual-apprehension core is broad, distinctive (naZar-vs-bSr 7:198/10:43; 'ayn-vs-yubSir 7:195/36:66) and adversarially clean, and the sensory<->cognitive bridge is Quran-internal (6:104,22:46,13:16), so the core is not refuted (not FAILED) and RESISTANT/no-nucleus is not sustainable. But a coherent resistant lexicalized/factitive sub-class (baSaa'ir/baSiira-as-proof/tabSira/mubSir) genuinely resists a UNIFORM sense, so a clean SUPPORTED-with-empty-failing-occurrences run cannot be claimed: status is NOT_RUN with the resisting occurrences recorded.
